question.worked_solution:
First, recall the associative law

$$
ABC=(AB)C=A(BC).
$$

Notice that $A$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix, $B$ is a $2\times 3$ matrix, and $C$ is a $3\times 1$ matrix. Therefore, 

- multiplying $A$ by $B$, we will obtain a $3\times 3$ matrix, which will require finding $9$ entries, while

- multiplying $B$ by $C$, we will obtain a $2\times 1$ matrix, which will require finding $2$ entries.

So, we find the product $BC$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply $A$ by $BC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ABC & =A(BC) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ 6 \\ 28\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
